description: Opik LLM Traces Dashboard — shows every LLM API call made during automation workflows as structured traces with hierarchical spans, cost attribution, token counts, latency, and quality feedback scores. Users come here to answer: What did the AI do? How much did it cost? Was it effective? Data arrives from two sources: (1) the Opik REST API at OPIK_BASE_URL/v1/private/traces for trace/span data stored in ClickHouse, and (2) the runner's own /analytics/token-usage endpoints as a fallback when Opik is unavailable. A background sync service in the Rust backend pushes execution_spans and phase_token_usage records to Opik as traces/spans, and syncs observations and agentic_metric_scores as feedback scores. Opik runs as a self-hosted Docker stack (backend, ClickHouse, MySQL, Redis, MinIO) managed by the supervisor.
preconditions: Opik Docker services are running and healthy (GET OPIK_BASE_URL/health-check returns 200)
Runner has OPIK_BASE_URL configured in settings (default: http://localhost:5173/api)
PostgreSQL is available for the runner's local span/observation storage

groups.name: Architecture — Data Flow & Integration Design
groups.description:
How the Opik integration is structured. Data flows in one primary direction: the runner records execution_spans and phase_token_usage in PostgreSQL during workflow execution, then a background OpikSyncService pushes batches to Opik every 10 seconds. Observations are mapped to Opik feedback scores. The frontend queries Opik directly for the trace viewer and falls back to local analytics endpoints when Opik is unreachable. MCP tools (opik_traces, opik_trace_detail, opik_feedback, opik_evaluate, opik_sync_status) expose trace data to AI agents.

Data model mapping:
- task_run → Opik project (project_name = workflow_name)
- execution_spans (root, parent_span_id=NULL) → Opik trace
- execution_spans (child) → Opik span (preserves parent_span_id hierarchy)
- phase_token_usage → span.usage + span.model + span.provider + span.total_estimated_cost
- observations → feedback_score (name=observation_type, value=1.0 for learning / 0.0 for bugfix, reason=content)
- agentic_metric_scores → feedback_score (name=metric_type, value=score, reason=rationale)

Sync is idempotent via trace_id (UUIDv7). On restart, sync resumes from last_synced_at timestamp. Retry uses exponential backoff (1s→2s→4s→8s, max 60s). Unsent traces queue in memory (max 10,000) and overflow to PostgreSQL.

groups.name: Semantic — Purpose & Communication
groups.description: What the dashboard communicates to users. The page heading, status indicators, and summary cards orient users immediately: Is Opik connected? How many traces exist? What's the total cost? Each trace row provides a scannable summary (name, cost, tokens, duration, quality) so users can spot expensive or failing AI calls without clicking into details.

assertions.description: The page shows an 'LLM Traces' heading that orients users to the trace browser
assertions.expected: Heading text 'LLM Traces' is visible at the top of the content area

assertions.description: Users see a connection status badge indicating whether trace data is flowing from Opik
assertions.expected: Badge shows 'Connected' with green styling when Opik is reachable, or 'Disconnected' with red styling when unreachable

assertions.description: Users see each trace row displaying workflow name, total cost, input/output token counts, duration, and a quality indicator, enabling quick assessment of AI effectiveness
assertions.expected: Each row contains: workflow name (text), cost (dollar amount), tokens (formatted as 'N in / N out'), duration (human-readable), and quality badge (green >=0.7, yellow >=0.4, red <0.4)
assertions.precondition: At least one workflow has been executed and synced to Opik
assertions.notes: Quality badge value derived from averaged feedback scores on the trace

assertions.description: The cost summary cards give users a financial overview of AI usage for the selected time range
assertions.expected: Four cards visible: Total Cost (dollar amount), Avg Cost/Trace (dollar amount), Total Tokens (formatted number), Trace Count (integer)

groups.name: Element Presence — Required UI Controls
groups.description: All interactive controls that must exist for the dashboard to be functional. These elements are always present regardless of data state — they represent the page's chrome, not its content.

assertions.description: Users can access a time range selector to filter traces by recency
assertions.expected: Selector is visible with options: 1h, 6h, 24h, 7d, 30d

assertions.description: Users can access a search input for filtering traces by name, workflow, model, or tags
assertions.expected: Input is visible with placeholder text indicating search capability

assertions.description: Users can access filter controls to narrow traces by Model, Provider, Status, and Feedback Score range
The page shows a trace list table with sortable column headers
assertions.expected: Table visible with column headers: Name, Status, Cost, Tokens, Duration, Feedback, Created

assertions.description: Users can see a sync status indicator showing whether trace data is being pushed to Opik
assertions.expected: Indicator shows one of: 'Synced' (idle), 'Syncing' (active push), 'Queued: N' (pending traces), or 'Retrying' (connection lost)

assertions.description: The trace detail panel shows tabs for different views of the selected trace
assertions.expected: Tab bar with tabs: Spans, Input/Output, Metadata, Feedback
assertions.precondition: A trace row has been selected

assertions.description: Users can add manual feedback scores to a trace via a dedicated button
assertions.precondition: A trace row has been selected and the detail panel is open

assertions.description: Users can open the selected trace in Opik's full web UI for advanced analysis
assertions.precondition: A trace is selected and Opik connection status is 'Connected'

groups.name: Data Display — Formatting & Presentation
groups.description: How trace, span, cost, and feedback data is formatted for readability. Users scanning the trace list need to compare costs and durations quickly, so consistent formatting is essential. The span tree needs visual hierarchy to show the execution chain clearly.

assertions.description: The page shows cost values formatted as dollar amounts — 4 decimal places for individual traces (e.g., '$0.0042'), 2 decimal places for summary totals (e.g., '$1.23')
assertions.expected: Dollar sign prefix, appropriate decimal precision as described
assertions.precondition: At least one trace exists with cost data

assertions.description: The page shows token counts with thousand separators, distinguishing input from output (e.g., '12,450 in / 3,200 out')
assertions.expected: Two numbers separated by ' in / ' with thousand-separator commas
assertions.precondition: At least one trace exists with token data

assertions.description: The page shows duration in human-readable format: <1s as 'Xms', 1-60s as 'X.Xs', 1-60m as 'Xm Ys', >1h as 'Xh Ym'
assertions.expected: Duration text matches the appropriate tier format based on the actual value
assertions.precondition: At least one trace exists

assertions.description: The span tree shows a Gantt-style timeline bar for each span, proportional to its duration relative to the trace total, color-coded by span type
assertions.expected: Each span row has a horizontal bar whose width is proportional to span duration / trace duration. Colors: LLM spans use getAccentColors('blue'), tool spans use getAccentColors('green'), general spans use getAccentColors('zinc'), guardrail spans use getAccentColors('amber')
assertions.precondition: A trace is selected and the Spans tab is active in the detail panel

assertions.description: The page shows span input/output as syntax-highlighted JSON in a collapsible code block with a copy-to-clipboard button. JSON larger than 500 characters is collapsed by default
assertions.expected: Code block visible with syntax highlighting. Collapsed JSON shows a toggle button to expand. Expanded state persists until user collapses or selects a different span
assertions.precondition: A span is selected in the span tree

assertions.description: The page shows model and provider names as color-coded badges for quick visual identification
assertions.expected: Badge visible with provider-specific color. Text shows model name (e.g., 'claude-sonnet-4-20250514')
assertions.precondition: At least one trace exists with model data
assertions.notes: Color mapping: OpenAI=green, Anthropic=amber, Google=blue, local/other=gray

assertions.description: The page shows error traces with a red left border and truncated error message, distinguishing them visually from successful traces
assertions.expected: Row has a visible red left border (border-l-2 border-red-500 or similar). Error message text is truncated to one line with ellipsis. Full traceback available in the detail panel's Metadata tab
assertions.precondition: At least one trace exists with error_info populated

groups.name: Interaction — User Actions & Responses
groups.description: How users interact with the dashboard — searching, filtering, selecting traces, navigating the span tree, and adding feedback. Each interaction should feel responsive (<2s for local actions, <5s for Opik API calls).

assertions.description: Users can type in the search input and press Enter to filter traces by name
assertions.expected: After pressing Enter, the trace list updates within 2 seconds showing only traces whose name or workflow contains the search string (case-insensitive substring match). Empty search restores the full list

assertions.description: Users can click a trace row to open the detail panel showing the span tree and metadata
assertions.expected: Detail panel appears (or updates if already open) showing the selected trace's span tree in the Spans tab, with input/output, metadata, and feedback available via tabs. The selected row has a highlighted background (bg-primary/10 or similar)
assertions.precondition: At least one trace exists in the list

assertions.description: Users can click a span in the tree to view its details: input/output JSON, model, tokens, cost, duration, and errors
assertions.expected: Span detail section updates to show the selected span's input JSON, output JSON, model name, provider, input/output token counts, cost, duration, and error info (if any). Previously selected span loses its highlight
assertions.precondition: A trace is selected and the Spans tab is active

assertions.description: Users can change the time range to filter all dashboard data by recency
assertions.expected: Summary cards (Total Cost, Avg Cost, Tokens, Trace Count) update to reflect only traces within the selected window. Trace list filters accordingly. If the previously selected trace falls outside the new range, the detail panel closes

assertions.description: Users can expand and collapse span tree nodes to navigate the execution hierarchy
assertions.expected: Clicking the chevron toggles child span visibility. Collapsed parent shows a '(N spans)' count badge. Expanded parent shows indented child spans
assertions.precondition: A trace with nested spans (at least 2 levels deep) is selected

assertions.description: Users can add a feedback score to a trace by clicking 'Add Feedback', selecting a score name, entering a value, and submitting
assertions.expected: A form appears with: score name dropdown (relevance, accuracy, helpfulness, or custom text input), numeric value input (0.0-1.0), optional reason textarea, and Submit button. After submission, a new feedback score badge appears on the trace row and in the Feedback tab of the detail panel
assertions.precondition: A trace is selected and the detail panel is open
assertions.notes: Writes to both Opik (PUT /v1/private/traces/{id}/feedback-scores) and local observations (POST /observations with topic_key='feedback/{trace_id}/{name}')

assertions.description: Users can click column headers in the trace list to sort by that column
assertions.expected: First click sorts ascending (up arrow indicator), second click sorts descending (down arrow), third click clears sort. Trace list reorders accordingly
assertions.precondition: At least 2 traces exist in the list

groups.name: Behavior — Loading, Empty, Error, & Auto-refresh States
groups.description: Automatic behaviors and edge case handling. The dashboard must handle: first-time use (no data), Opik being unreachable, slow API responses, and ongoing data arrival from background sync.

assertions.description: When no traces exist, the page shows an empty state guiding users on how data will appear
assertions.expected: Empty state message visible with text indicating traces will appear after running a workflow. No error indicators, no broken layout
assertions.precondition: No workflows have been executed, or Opik has no trace data for the current time range

assertions.description: When Opik is unreachable, the page gracefully falls back to local data with a visible fallback banner
assertions.expected: Yellow/amber banner visible with text 'Showing local data — Opik unavailable'. Dashboard displays data from runner's /analytics endpoints. No JavaScript errors in console. Connection status badge shows 'Disconnected' (red)
assertions.precondition: Opik Docker services are stopped or OPIK_BASE_URL is unreachable

assertions.description: The trace list uses infinite scroll pagination, loading additional traces as the user scrolls near the bottom
assertions.expected: Initially displays up to 50 traces. When user scrolls within 200px of the bottom, the next page loads automatically. A loading spinner appears briefly during fetch. Total trace count visible in summary card
assertions.precondition: More than 50 traces exist in the selected time range

assertions.description: The dashboard refreshes trace data periodically so users see recent traces without manual reload
assertions.expected: New traces appear in the list within 30 seconds of the background sync completing, without user action
assertions.precondition: A workflow has just completed and traces were synced to Opik

groups.name: State Consistency — Local ↔ Opik Data Agreement
groups.description: The dashboard shows data from two sources: Opik (primary) and the runner's local database (fallback). These must agree when both are available, and the fallback must be seamless when Opik is down.

assertions.description: The summary card trace count matches the number of visible rows in the trace list (accounting for pagination)
assertions.expected: The 'Trace Count' summary card value equals the total number of traces (which may exceed visible rows if paginated). Total Cost card equals the sum of individual trace costs
assertions.precondition: At least one trace exists

assertions.description: Feedback scores added in the runner appear in the Opik web UI, and scores added in Opik appear in the runner dashboard
assertions.expected: A feedback score added in the runner's Feedback tab appears in Opik's trace detail within 10 seconds. Conversely, a score added in Opik's UI appears in the runner's dashboard on the next auto-refresh cycle (≤30s)
assertions.precondition: Opik is connected and a trace with feedback scores exists
assertions.notes: Runner→Opik: immediate PUT on creation. Opik→Runner: polled on auto-refresh interval

assertions.description: After a workflow execution completes, its trace appears in the dashboard within 15 seconds
assertions.expected: The most recent trace in the list corresponds to the just-completed workflow, with correct name, cost, and token data. Appears within 15 seconds (sync batch interval 10s + API latency)
assertions.precondition: A workflow execution has just completed

groups.name: Navigation — Page Access & Internal Navigation
groups.description: How users reach the Opik dashboard and navigate within it. The page is a tab in the OBSERVE sidebar group. Internal navigation is panel-based (trace list + detail panel), not route-based.

assertions.description: The 'LLM Traces' tab is accessible from the OBSERVE group in the sidebar
assertions.expected: Button labeled 'LLM Traces' is visible in the sidebar's OBSERVE section. Clicking it loads the Opik dashboard in the main content area

assertions.description: Users can navigate between trace detail tabs without losing the selected trace
assertions.expected: Clicking Spans, Input/Output, Metadata, or Feedback tabs switches the detail content while preserving the selected trace. The active tab has a distinct visual treatment (underline or background color)
assertions.precondition: A trace row has been selected and the detail panel is open

assertions.description: Users can dismiss the trace detail panel and return to the full-width list view
assertions.expected: Pressing Escape or clicking a close/X button hides the detail panel. The trace list expands to fill the available width. No trace row remains highlighted
assertions.precondition: The detail panel is currently open with a trace selected

groups.name: Style — Visual Design & Theming
groups.description: The Opik dashboard must visually integrate with the runner's existing dark theme and design system. No Opik-branded colors or styles should leak through — it should feel native to the runner.

assertions.description: The dashboard uses the runner's dark theme tokens consistently
assertions.expected: Background uses bg-background (dark). Text uses text-foreground. Borders use border-border. No white backgrounds, no Opik purple branding, no light-theme leakage

assertions.description: The connection status badge uses the runner's status color system
assertions.expected: Connected: getStatusColors('success') — green background/text. Disconnected: getStatusColors('error') — red. Syncing: getStatusColors('warning') — yellow/amber

assertions.description: Trace list rows have alternating backgrounds and hover feedback
assertions.expected: Even rows transparent, odd rows bg-muted/10. Hover state: bg-muted/50. Selected row: bg-primary/10 with border-primary/30
assertions.precondition: At least 2 traces exist in the list

states.name: Loading — Initial Data Fetch
states.description: The dashboard is loading. A health check to Opik determines connection status, and the initial trace list and summary stats are being fetched. Time range selector and search input are present but disabled until data arrives.

target.condition: Opik responds with zero traces for the selected time range
Opik returns one or more traces

transitions.name: Opik Unreachable — Fallback to Local Data

target.condition: Opik health check fails or OPIK_BASE_URL unreachable

states.name: Empty State — No Traces Yet
states.description: Opik is connected but no traces exist for the selected time range. An empty state message guides users that traces will appear after running a workflow. Summary cards show zero values. Controls (time range, search, filters) are enabled.

target.condition: Auto-refresh detects new traces within 30 seconds

states.name: Trace List — Browsing Traces
states.description: The main dashboard view showing the trace list with summary cards (Total Cost, Avg Cost/Trace, Total Tokens, Trace Count), connection status badge (green/Connected), sync status indicator, and all filter controls enabled. Each trace row shows workflow name, cost, tokens (in/out), duration, quality badge, and model/provider badges. Infinite scroll loads more traces near the bottom.

target.condition: Opik health check fails during auto-refresh

states.name: Trace Detail — Span Tree & Metadata
states.description: A trace row is selected and the detail panel is open alongside the trace list. The panel shows tabs: Spans (Gantt-style timeline with hierarchical span tree), Input/Output (JSON viewer), Metadata (model, error info), and Feedback (score badges, Add Feedback button). Individual spans can be clicked for detail. The Open in Opik button is available when connected.

states.name: Fallback Mode — Opik Unavailable
states.description: Opik is unreachable. The dashboard displays a yellow/amber fallback banner ('Showing local data — Opik unavailable'), connection status badge shows 'Disconnected' (red), and data is served from the runner's local /analytics endpoints. All dashboard functionality remains available with local data. The system periodically retries connecting to Opik.

target.condition: Opik health check succeeds on retry

backendFiles: qontinui-runner/src-tauri/src/opik/sync_service.rs — Background trace sync to Opik (batch push every 10s)
qontinui-runner/src/services/opik-service.ts — Frontend API service (fetches from Opik or falls back to local)
qontinui-runner/src/hooks/useOpikTraces.ts — React hook for trace list with search/filter/pagination
qontinui-mcp/src/qontinui_mcp/server.py — MCP tools (opik_traces, opik_trace_detail, opik_feedback, opik_evaluate, opik_sync_status)
apiEndpoints: Opik REST: GET /v1/private/traces — List traces (paginated, filtered by project/time/name)
Opik REST: GET /v1/private/traces/{id} — Single trace with aggregated feedback scores
Opik REST: GET /v1/private/spans?trace_id={id} — Spans for a trace (hierarchical via parent_span_id)
Opik REST: POST /v1/private/traces/batch — Batch create/update traces (used by sync service)
Opik REST: POST /v1/private/spans/batch — Batch create/update spans
Opik REST: PUT /v1/private/traces/{id}/feedback-scores — Set feedback score on a trace
Opik REST: GET /v1/private/traces/stats — Aggregated statistics for summary cards
Opik REST: GET /health-check — Backend health check
Runner HTTP: GET /opik/sync-status — Sync service status (pending/synced counts, last_synced_at)
Runner HTTP: GET /analytics/token-usage/summary — Fallback: local cost/token summary
Runner HTTP: GET /analytics/token-usage/daily — Fallback: local daily breakdown
Tauri: search_opik_traces(query: String, time_range: String, page: u32) → Vec<OpikTrace>
Tauri: get_opik_trace_detail(trace_id: String) → OpikTraceDetail (trace + spans + feedback)
Tauri: add_opik_feedback(trace_id: String, name: String, value: f64, reason: Option<String>) → Result<()>
